This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<tools-used-before-summary>Agent, Bash, Edit, Read, SendMessage, SendUserFile, ToolSearch, WebSearch, Write, mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task, mcp__ccd_session__start_session, mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__list_events, mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan, mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up</tools-used-before-summary>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Kenneth is designing the pricing/credits experience for JusPrin 2's hosted AI chat (JusPrin Cloud gateway). Settled model: unit "credits" (~2¢), Basic message 1 credit, Expert message 5; plans Hobby ($10/mo, 750 credits), Workshop ($20/mo, 1,000 credits + "unlimited" Basic up to a placeholder 600), Pay as you go (500 credits/$10, never expire); "your first month" 500-credit grant (never "trial"); trickle placeholder 50 basic-only/month; Obico subscribers 20% off subscriptions; rewards 25 credits per print report. In this stretch he asked, in order: (a) implicitly, to relay the design session's board captures for his review (continuing "capture your design and display them here so that I can review them"); (b) "After my review" — wait until his canvas review is done before re-rendering and syncing the docs; (c) whether to keep the dedicated "Credits & plans" canvas page or move boards back to their flow pages ("tell the sub session to put them back" after my recommendation to fold them back); (d) an architecture opinion: server APIs for subscription/credits vs account/subscription pages served directly from the server into a webview (his reasons: pricing experiments without app releases, no old versions interfering; he asked for downsides); (e) the standing task of syncing `pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md` and `pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md` to the final boards.
   Standing constraints (preserved): use `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for gcloud/kubectl, read-only on production; never commit submodules; working docs stay untracked and are never hidden via .gitignore/.git/info/exclude; no attribution lines in commits/PRs; no live-model spend without a stated batch Kenneth approves; keys never printed; Kenneth's pricing corrections stand (v1 low usage = low stickiness, v1 figures are floors; rewards don't invite gaming in this audience; Obico lifetime conversion ≈5%, renewal ≈77%); every allowance/ceiling sentence needs an engaged-usage source or the word "placeholder"; direct opinions, no filler questions.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Canvas: JusPrin v2 design canvas artifact https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, now at version 70 (1793601849-6e47); boards moved to flow pages in v69: "On boarding experience" (1a,1b,1c,1d,6a,6b), "Compositions" beside the Composer (2a,2b,2c,3a,3b,3c,3d,7a,7b,7c), "Agent setup & Preferences" (4a,4b,4c), "Print history" (8a,8b,8c,8d), "Credits & plans" (board 0 five rules, 5a, 5b, 9). Boards carry "Credits · " in canvas names; builder places via a LAYOUT table. Dark variants exist only as PNGs (4a has none).
   - Review decisions (Kenneth, 2026-11-02): a chat keeps its model (pickers greyed with two-line tooltip, board 2c); prices always "N credits a message"; composer shows only a ring, count in hover panel ("just like how claude code behaves"); a progress bar per kind of expiring credit (fill = what is left, ChatGPT's way); "Get more credits" is the one action outside the pricing page (savings alert keeps "Subscribe"); no "New Basic chat" under 5 spendable credits (board 3d = only case: free Basic messages left); sign-up offer as headline + button "Sign in for 500 credits"; "Your own API key"; v1 subscribers grandfathered to Hobby at original price ($6.99/mo or $59.99/yr) plus the 500; "Obico Premium Subscriber" wording; report button lives in Print history (8a) and Home project card (8d), not the chat marker; confirmation row "Report sent · 16:10 · 25 credits added" (8c).
   - Open (session's fill-ins / Kenneth unanswered): bought credits with no bar; what the ring measures against (placeholder 61% vs 58% of 1,050); whether "1 credit" was confusing for unit or word; v1 move timing (sign-in vs term end) and "unlimited" wording; New Basic chat carrying only typed text / whether 3d stays; Home line two-week limit; report button on export-only entries; rule 5 wording and rule 1's missing plan-names sentence on board 0; stray "Your text here" box on 1a; label for unspent reward lots (never expire, not bought); default tier after first month; reverse alert on/off; webview vs in-app pages.
   - Example balance (v70): 62 first-month + 50 free Basic + 500 bought = 612 = "612 Basic or 112 Expert messages" (Expert count excludes basic-only credits); alert: 820 credits = $16.40 PAYG vs $11.40 Hobby ($10 + 70×2¢) → saving $5.00.
   - Architecture recommendation (section 5.4): composer on API (`/account`, `/models` with per-alias `credits`); Account + pricing as server pages in a second AgentWebView; `POST /ent/jusprin/v2/webview_session` returns single-use 60 s login URL (never token in URL); `?theme=` + same token CSS; checkout stays in system browser; bridge messages `credits_changed`, `close`; offline state; Steam precedent.
   - 402 body: `{"balance": 3, "cost": 5, "basic_only_credits": 0, "affordable_aliases": ["slicer-basic"], "plan": null}`; `basic_only_credits` ≥ 5 drives "New Basic chat".
   - Obico naming data: tsd-enterprise strings "Pro plan"/"Pro Plan"/"Obico Pro Plan" 284 vs "Premium plan"/"Premium Plan" 67; "AI Premium" is the Chargebee plan's internal name.
   - Memories written by the design session: chat-keeps-its-model, usage-against-quota-common-shape, one-action-to-get-more-credits, credit-price-needs-its-unit, sign-up-reason-must-be-prominent, render-canvas-boards-with-render-dc.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md` (untracked; rewritten wholesale with Write, then edited; header "synced to canvas version 70 on 2026-11-02"). Contents: board placement paragraph; five rules (rule 1 with "612 credits left. That is 612 Basic or 112 Expert messages" and the (612 − 50)/5 note; rule 3 examples "First-month credits · 62 of 500 left · Expires 1 Dec", "Bought credits · 500 left · Never expire"; rule 5 with note that the session dropped "a way to send it anyway"); "Two decisions from the review" section (chat keeps its model; Get more credits); points 1–12 rewritten to boards (1a–1d incl. v1 line on 1c and 1d wording; 2b/2c picker + tooltip; 2a/4a–4c ring + bars + Usage shape; 3a–3d pre-send/failed card; 4c/5a fair use "188 of 600 left"; 7a–7c alert "$5.00" with $11.40 sums; 5a/5b pricing page card wording + webview note; 6a/6b; 8a–8d; 11; 12 Obico Premium Subscriber with Pro footnote); "Open for Kenneth" list (11 items incl. reward-lot label); "Decided" paragraph.
   - `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md` (untracked; edited). Changes: line 9 translated-balance sentence (112); section 3.4 price per alias not per effort; section 3.2 402 body with `basic_only_credits`; section 4 v1 subscribers bullet (decided: Hobby at original price via plan change + per-customer forever coupon; open timing/wording; 20 subs) and pricing page bullet (boards 5a/5b, served by webview if 5.4 accepted); section 5.1 `/account` JSON:
     ```json
     "credits": {"total": 612, "lots": [
         {"kind": "signup", "credits": 62, "granted": 500, "expires_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z"},
         {"kind": "trickle", "credits": 50, "granted": 50, "basic_only": true, "expires_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z"},
         {"kind": "pack", "credits": 500, "granted": 500, "expires_at": null}]},
     ...
     "usage_30d": {"basic_turns": 140, "expert_turns": 60, "credits": 440,
                   "days": [{"date": "2026-11-19", "credits": 60}, ...],
                   "activity": [{"date": "2026-11-19", "chat": "...", "tier": "expert", "messages": 12, "credits": 60},
                                {"date": "2026-11-18", "kind": "report_removed", "title": "Print report · Vent Grille", "credits": -25, "note": "The photo doesn't show a printed object."}]}
     ```
     Section 5.2 rewritten ("Synced to canvas version 70"): chat keeps its model (`Composer.tsx` disable once chat has a message; `chat-history-cache-plan.md` D5 superseded), picker wording, balance ring/panel (`granted`, reward-lot label gap, 112 note), before sending (Send disabled, "Get more credits", "New Basic chat" when ≥5 free Basic), exhaustion card, Preferences › Account, BYOK, design (two-line tooltip needs token change). New section 5.4 "Where the Account and pricing pages render (recommend: the server)". Section 8 rewards (button in Print history + Home card, form fields, 8c row, clawback row with reason). Section 11 steps 2, 3, 5 updated. Section 12 decisions: 1 (Expert then Basic vs last chosen), 8 (decided; open timing/wording), 11 (Premium is Kenneth's; Pro note), 12 (webview), 13 (no bar / ring total / reward-lot label), 14 (New Basic chat / 3d); "Decided during the review" paragraph.
   - `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/design-captures/credits-2026-11/` — 35 PNGs at v70 (credits-00-rules, 01a–01d (+dark), 02a–02c, 03a–03d, 04a, 04b(+dark), 04c(+dark), 05a(+dark), 05b, 06a, 06b, 07a–07c, 08a–08d, 09(+dark)).
   - `/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_756f4482-e5c7-45b4-bc36-5e6db3b079ef/credits-boards-changelog-v54-to-v69.md` — the design session's changelog (read; source for attributions and the three arithmetic errors).
   - Read-only: memory files listed above; `jusprin-cloud-provider.md` memory.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Attribution errors in my first sync (fixed from the changelog): I had recorded "never-expiring credits have no bar" and rule 5's phrase drop as decisions; both were the session's calls, now marked open. I had framed "Obico Premium Subscriber" as open with my Pro recommendation; it was Kenneth's explicit wording, now recorded as his with a footnote. I had framed the v1 Hobby grandfathering as the board's position; it was Kenneth's decision on board 1c.
   - Three arithmetic errors in boards and docs (session found): "122 Expert" → 112; "$6.40" → "$5.00" with $11.40; 450 bought beside 112 first-month impossible → balance changed to 62+50+500 on canvas v70; docs updated.
   - `affordable_aliases` non-empty was the wrong test for "New Basic chat"; added `basic_only_credits` to the 402 body.
   - Plan called the Lovable one-meter shape current; the changelog showed bars replaced it in v59; docs now describe bars.
   - Earlier: wrap_up recaps must stay ≤300 chars.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Relayed each design-session turn to Kenneth in one or two lines with captures; recommended and executed (via the session) moving boards to flow pages; answered the server-vs-API architecture question with a split recommendation; produced a full two-document sync to canvas v70 grounded in the session's changelog rather than memory; got the three wrong numbers fixed on the boards.
   - Noted but not yet actioned (session's "left as they were"): board 0 rule 3 example still "112 first-month credits"; board 9 "388 first-month credits expire"; ring 61% vs placeholder 58%; launch offer date; orange note on Credits & plans saying docs allow mid-chat switch is out of date.

6. All user messages:
   - "After my review"
   - "The design looks good now. But should we keep this new page or should we put the board back to the original flow they belong to? For instance, the boards of our bowling go back to The onboarding experience page. Or is keeping plan/credit-related boards on a dedicated a best practice?"
   - "tell the sub session to put them back"
   - "is it a good idea to have the server provide the subscription/credit through apis, or is it better to have the account/subscription pages to be directly loaded from the server? I believe the biggest advantage of the account/subscription pages being directly loaded from the server is that We may need to experiment with the pricing etc. a lot. And hence, it can be a lot easier for us to update without releasing a new version. Also, it's a lot easier for us to make sure that no old versions are interfering with the latest version. any downside for serving those pages directly from server into a webview in the app?"
   - (Kenneth's canvas-thread comments, relayed via the design session's changelog, are quoted in section 2 and are his decisions, not chat messages.)

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Kenneth's answer to the wrap-up ask "Start step 1, the gateway credit ledger, now?" (asked three times, unanswered) — do not start implementation without it.
   - Kenneth's open decisions (plan section 12 items 1, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14 and the open parts of 8; design doc "Open for Kenneth" list).
   - Possible board clean-ups the session left (board 0 rule 3 example, board 9 example, ring %, launch date, orange note) — not requested; mention if relevant.
   - Earlier offers still open: count Obico's `PrintShotFeedbackReview.invalid` share; harness fix 01ec46a4af on `refs/heads/claude/journey-anthropic-provider` unmerged (merge only if Kenneth says so).

8. Current Work:
   The doc sync to canvas version 70 was just completed. Last actions: a python script updated both docs' example balance to 62/50/500, added `granted` to the `/account` lots, bumped "canvas version 69" → "70", added the unspent-reward-lot question to the design doc's open list and plan decision 13; verified the only remaining "450" is the explanatory "450 of 500 bar" example in point 3; called wrap_up with recap "Canvas version 70 fixes the three sums (112 Expert, $5.00 saving, a 62 + 50 + 500 balance with a purchase row) and both working docs now match it. One new gap is listed for you: what the balance panel calls an unspent reward lot..." and the ask "Start step 1, the gateway credit ledger, now?" The closing message to Kenneth after that wrap_up had not yet been written when the summary request arrived.

9. Optional Next Step:
   Write the short closing message for the completed turn (both docs match canvas v70; the reward-lot label gap is new; the session left board 0/board 9 examples and the ring percentage as they were), then wait for Kenneth's answer on "Start step 1, the gateway credit ledger, now?" before any implementation. If he says yes, step 1 per the plan's section 11: ledger tables, `charge_turn`, draw order, lazy trickle, sign-up lot, `credits_exhausted` 402 body with `basic_only_credits`, `tier`/`credits`/`images` in aliases, `slicer-basic` alias, `/account` — in tsd-enterprise in its own worktree, with the tests listed there.

If you need specific details from before compaction (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: /Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/aee0a899-9c4e-4dbf-9722-e90cbcd70923.jsonl
Continue the conversation from where it left off without asking the user any further questions. Resume directly — do not acknowledge the summary, do not recap what was happening, do not preface with "I'll continue" or similar. Pick up the last task as if the break never happened.

The messages after this summary are the most recent messages from before compaction, kept verbatim. The summary was written without seeing them, so something it says has not happened yet may already have happened in them.

The design session [Draw the credits and plans screens on the canvas](#local_b14d4c8e-5962-47f4-93d0-a36258ec6863) published canvas version 70 with the three sums fixed, and both working docs now match it.

**What changed on the boards.** The translated balance reads "612 Basic or 112 Expert messages" on 2a, 4a and 4b. The savings alert on 7a and 7b reads "$5.00", and 7b spells out "$11.40 on Hobby ($10 plus 70 more credits at 2¢ each)". To make the bought credits consistent with "expiring credits are used first", the example balance is now 62 first-month + 50 free Basic + 500 bought = 612, and 4b's usage table gained a "Bought 500 credits · +500" row dated 17 Nov in the same list as chats. The re-rendered captures are under the same names in `design-captures/credits-2026-11/`.

**What changed in the docs.** The example lots in the `/account` JSON and in both docs' balance examples now use 62, 50 and 500, each lot carries its `granted` size for the bars, and the "being corrected" notes are gone.

**One new gap the fix exposed**, now listed for you in both docs: a person with an unspent 25-credit reward holds credits that never expire but were not bought. No board shows that case, and "Bought credits" is the wrong label for it, so the balance panel needs a name for a reward lot.

**Left as they were on the canvas**, by the session's report: board 0's rule 3 and board 9 keep their own example states, the composer ring stays at 61% while its rule is a placeholder, the launch offer's 31 Jan date is a placeholder, and the orange note on the Credits & plans page still says the docs allow a mid-chat model switch, which is now out of date.

Still a few things to consider:

* Is there a better phrase than "Basic Message"? I think "Expert" is good enough.
* deepseek v4 flash doesn't support image, we need to show user "if you want to let the agent see the picture, use "Expert". 
* when user just opened an extenral file, we will have the agent to automatically respond to that open. it should be sonnet (expert) model because it needs to read 3d render view. But currently we let the user choose model when they send the first message.  which model do we use to do the automated response?
Three design questions; I'll check what the two working docs already say about each before answering.

result.output:
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:7:What the survey of other products (`pricing-case-studies-2026-10.md`) says goes wrong, in one list: people cannot picture what an abstract credit buys; two kinds of credit with different expiry rules confuse everyone; the anger is at the boundary, when something they were doing stops; a balance that drops for reasons they did not cause breeds distrust; "unlimited" with an unstated ceiling is read as a lie once reached.
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:11:1. **One word, one unit, always translated.** "Credits" (decided 2026-11-01), never coins, never tokens. A credit is explained once, in messages: "an Expert message is 5 credits, a Basic message is 1". Every balance is shown translated, "612 credits left. That is 612 Basic or 112 Expert messages", so nobody converts in their head. The Expert count leaves out credits that only Basic can spend: 612 credits of which 50 are free Basic messages is (612 − 50) / 5 = 112, not 122 (the first boards said 122; fixed in canvas version 70). A price never stands alone: "1 credit" confused Kenneth on sight (2026-11-02), so it is always "1 credit a message", "5 credits a message". Dollars appear only on the page where money changes hands. Plans are Hobby ($10 a month), Workshop ($20 a month) and Pay as you go (the never-expiring pack); never Pro, Plus or Premium.
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:12:2. **Credits only move when the person sends a message.** Turns the app starts (the file-opened report, the slice-finished note) are free, and the balance never changes without a message from the person. That one fact is what makes the balance trustworthy; it is stated on the pricing page in one sentence: "Only messages you send cost credits."
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:13:3. **Expiring credits are named by what they are, with a date. Bought credits are just "credits" and never expire.** "First-month credits · 62 of 500 left · Expires 1 Dec." "Free Basic messages · 50 of 50 left · Resets 1 Dec." "Bought credits · 500 left · Never expire." Never a bare number that mixes them. The draw rule is stated once, in the breakdown: "Expiring credits are used first."
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:15:5. **Nothing typed is lost and nothing stops silently.** A message that cannot be sent stays in the composer. (The earlier draft added "with a way to send it anyway"; the design session dropped the phrase on board 0 because a chat now keeps its model, so there is no way to send. That follows from Kenneth's decision but he has not reviewed the wording. The ways forward are to get more credits or, when free Basic messages remain, to start a Basic chat with the typed text carried over.)
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:19:- **A chat keeps its model.** Kenneth, 2026-11-02, board 3b: for now a person cannot switch the model mid-chat. The model and thinking pickers stay in the composer once a chat has a message, greyed, and hovering either shows a two-line tooltip: "A chat keeps the model and thinking level it started with. Start a new chat to change them." and "Each message you send in this chat costs 5 credits." (board 2c). So there is no "Send with Basic" and no "Switch this chat to Basic" anywhere.
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:28:Kenneth's reaction to the first draft, which put the offer as a small line under "Set up JusPrin": "the most non-obvious way to urge user to sign up". Opinion, as drawn: the offer is the headline on its own surface, "Your first month: 500 credits", with the translation under it, "That is 500 Basic or 100 Expert messages. Your own API key stays free.", and the button names the reward, "Sign in for 500 credits". "Explore first" moves below it. Never "trial" (decided): a trial promises a wall at the end. No dollar figure. The same hierarchy is on the setup row (1a), the welcome screen (1b) and the welcome-back window for a returning v1 user (1c), where signing in is the primary button and Continue secondary. It is "Your own API key", not "your own key" (Kenneth, board 1a).
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:30:v1 subscribers (Kenneth, board 1c: "make it clear that JusPrin v1 subscribers grandfathered to the $10/mo tier with the original price", "in addition to getting 500 credits"). 1c adds the line "Subscribed to JusPrin v1? You get these 500 credits and keep your original price, on the $10 Hobby plan.", conditional because the app cannot know until sign-in. Board 1d is what that person sees once signed in: "Hobby, at your original $6.99 a month. 750 credits a month: 750 Basic or 150 Expert messages. Plus 500 more for your first month. New subscribers pay $10. You keep this price while subscribed." Nothing to choose, no upgrade prompt; the annual plan reads "at your original $59.99 a year". The design session's fill-ins, not yet confirmed: the price holds "while subscribed"; the 500 stack on the 750 in the first month; and when the move happens (at sign-in or at term end) and how to say that v1 was "unlimited" and Hobby is not are open. v1 has 20 active subscriptions, 15 annual and 5 monthly.
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:32:### 2. Picking Basic or Expert for a chat (boards 2b, 2c)
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:34:Where: the model picker in the composer (`ModelPickers.tsx`), chosen before the first message of a chat.
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:36:Opinion: each option gets the price with its unit and one plain clause about when to use it: "Basic · 1 credit a message · setting up an ordinary print" and "Expert · 5 credits a message · troubleshooting, tricky models, anything you'd ask a person". No model names, no vendor names: the person is choosing how much help to buy, not which company's model. On Basic the price reads "free this month" while free Basic messages last. On the person's own API key there is no price line. After the first message both pickers stay where they are, greyed, with the tooltip from the decision above.
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:38:Default for a new chat: Expert while the first-month credits last, because the first weeks decide whether the person stays. After that, Basic (board 6a). Whether a later new chat takes the last chosen tier instead is still open. Thinking levels (Fast, Thorough) are drawn at one price per tier; Expert defaults to Thorough and Basic to Fast (the design session's fill-in).
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:44:Kenneth, on the first draft's sentence-and-lines popover: "Don't reinvent the wheel", and later, with screenshots of Claude's and ChatGPT's usage screens, that both converge on a progress bar per kind of credit. Opinion, as drawn: in the composer only a small ring of what is left, "just like how claude code behaves", with no number beside it and no animation. Hovering or tapping it opens the panel: the total, translated ("612 credits left. That is 612 Basic or 112 Expert messages."), then one bar per kind of credit with what is left and its date, soonest to expire first ("First-month credits · 62 of 500 left · Expires 1 Dec"; "Free Basic messages · 50 of 50 left · Resets 1 Dec"). Every bar's fill is what is left, ChatGPT's way. Bought credits are drawn as a plain number with no bar ("Bought credits · 500 left · Never expire"); Kenneth asked why they get no bar, the design session recommended the plain number because there is no limit to measure against and a "450 of 500" bar would change its 500 on every top-up, and he has not answered, so this is open. What the ring itself measures against is also open (the board uses every credit in the balance when each kind started, a placeholder). One line, "Expiring credits are used first.", then "Get more credits" and "See usage". A person with only their own API key sees no ring.
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:46:The example balance is 62 first-month + 50 free Basic + 500 bought = 612 (canvas version 70; the first boards had 450 bought beside 112 first-month, which "expiring credits are used first" makes impossible). The usage table shows the purchase as a row, "Bought 500 credits · +500", in the same list as chats and rewards. One gap the example exposed: an unspent 25-credit reward never expires but is not bought, so it has no row in the balance panel and "Bought credits" is the wrong label for it; open for Kenneth.
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:48:Preferences › Account (4b, 4c) carries the same panel plus: the plan line ("Workshop · $16 a month. Renews 1 Dec."), "Manage plan" and "Get more credits", and Usage in Lovable's shape: a total for the last 30 days, a bar chart per day, and a table of chats with date, chat name, tier, messages and credits, including reward and clawback rows ("Print report · Vent Grille · +25", and a "−25" row with its reason, "Removed: the photo doesn't show a printed object."). "Where did my credits go" has an answer the person can look up alone.
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:54:First-month credits expire after 30 days, subscription credits at month end, the free Basic allowance at month end. Opinion: the panel always shows the date beside each expiring lot, as a bar. One notice, seven days before a lot expires, inside the composer area once: "388 first-month credits expire on 1 Dec." Never an email for this. When the lot has expired, nothing says "you lost 388 credits"; the panel simply shows what remains. Losing something you did not pay for should not be dramatised.
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:62:"New Basic chat" appears in one case only (3d): the person has free Basic messages left, which can pay for Basic but not for this Expert chat. The line reads "This Expert chat needs 5 credits a message. Your free Basic messages can only pay for Basic." with "Get more credits" and "New Basic chat"; the new chat opens on Basic with the typed text in its box and no earlier messages, so the earlier chat's context is lost (the design session's fill-in; Kenneth has not reviewed 3d, and if he drops New Basic chat altogether the board goes away). Under 5 credits there is no New Basic chat, because, as Kenneth put it, "if a user has <5 credits, no point for new basic chat here": it would run out within a few messages. Bought and plan credits pay for either tier, so only free Basic messages reach this case.
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:66:### 6. Unlimited Basic and its ceiling (boards 4c, 5a)
pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:70:Risk: "unlimited" that stops at a ceiling reads as a lie. Opinion: never write "unlimited" alone. The Workshop card says "Unlimited Basic messages for one person using JusPrin by hand, up to 600 a month; after that, 1 credit each." Account shows the ceiling as a bar like any other lot: "Free Basic messages · 188 of 600 left · Resets 1 Dec. After 600, Basic is 1 credit a message until then." A Basic message under the ceiling shows as 0 credits in the usage table. At 500, one notice. At 600, the picker's tooltip price changes to "1 credit a message" with one line saying why. pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md:84:Risk: the bounce to a browser, and the silence when the person returns ("did it go through?"). input.recap: Three recommendations: rename Basic to Quick, tell people a Quick chat cannot see pictures at the moment they attach one and in the picker, and run app-started turns like the file-opened report on Expert for free without pinning the chat. Nothing is written to the docs or boards yet.

content.text:
Three opinions, one per question.

**1. "Basic" → "Quick".** "Basic" sells the cheaper tier on a negative: it is the lesser one. "Quick" sells it on what it is good at, and it is honest, since the model is faster. That is how Perplexity (Quick vs Pro) and the Gemini app name the same split. It also reads better everywhere the word appears: "Unlimited Quick messages, up to 600 a month", "612 Quick or 112 Expert messages", "50 free Quick messages this month", "New Quick chat". "Standard" is the usual alternative, but it implies Expert is an upgrade from normal, and in the first month Expert is the default. One collision to fix: the thinking levels are Fast and Thorough, and "Quick with Fast thinking" sounds redundant. I would show the thinking picker only on Expert, since the cheap tier has one price anyway.

**2. The no-pictures model.** Do not rely on the model saying it cannot see the photo. Say it in two places before credits move. In the picker, the Quick option carries it as its clause: "Quick · 1 credit a message · text only, can't see pictures". In the composer, the moment a picture is attached in a Quick chat, a line under the attachment: "Quick can't see pictures. To show it to the agent, start an Expert chat." with a "New Expert chat" button that carries the text and the attachment, the same shape as board 3d's "New Basic chat". The gateway still strips image blocks and leaves a text note, as the plan says, so a photo that slips through costs nothing extra and the model knows one was dropped. One more host change follows: a Quick chat should not list `view_render` and the other picture-returning tools at all, keyed on the `images` flag the gateway reports per model, or the model calls a tool whose result it cannot read.

**3. The automatic reply when a file opens.** Today the app-started turn takes the chat's model, falls back to the account default (Expert), and pins the chat to it on that first request. So once pickers grey out after the first message, the person never chooses for a chat that began with a file, which is most project chats. My pick: the app's own turns are the app's, not the person's. They run on Expert, because the report needs the render, they cost nothing (rule 2 already says so, and the margin table already counts them, since everything runs on Sonnet today), and they do not pin the chat. The chat's model is fixed by the person's first message, and the greyed pickers follow that. A chat then has at most one Expert turn before a Quick one, in a known place, and the gateway already handles Quick reading an Expert turn's history by stripping the images. The alternative, pinning file-opened chats to Expert, makes Quick nearly unreachable and the Workshop ceiling meaningless. In code this is `use_chat_model` not storing the choice when the turn's origin is the app, and the app turn using the account's Expert alias directly.

Another Claude session sent a message:
<cross-session-message from="local_7448b3b2-e5e7-41e6-bd7d-8389f145dddf" from-name="JusPrin pricing model brainstorm">
Kenneth decided three things in a forked side session on 2026-11-02; record them in both working docs and have the design session apply them to the boards.

1. The cheap tier is called "Standard", not "Basic" (and not "Quick"). Every surface changes: picker "Standard · 1 credit a message", "Unlimited Standard messages", "612 Standard or 112 Expert messages", "50 free Standard messages this month", "New Standard chat", rule 1's explanation. Open point he did not rule on: the thinking picker on the Standard tier. My suggestion was to show the thinking picker only on Expert, since Standard has one price anyway.

2. Pictures in a Standard chat (DeepSeek v4 flash cannot see images). Kenneth rejected a long clause in the picker option. Decided: the picker option stays short. The notice lives on the staged attachment row itself, in the composer's existing attachment chip (AttachmentChip.tsx, which already has a thumbnail, a name line, a second line, and a Remove button). In a Standard chat a staged picture keeps its thumbnail, its second line reads "Standard can't see pictures, so this one will not be sent.", and the row gets a "New Expert chat" button beside Remove that starts an Expert chat carrying the typed text and the attachment (same shape as board 3d's new-chat button). Send stays enabled; the picture is simply dropped from the request (the gateway already strips image blocks for images:false backends and leaves a text note). This covers the + menu, drag-and-drop and paste, so the + menu needs no change. Host change that still follows: a Standard chat's tool list leaves out the picture-returning tools (view_render and friends), keyed on the per-model images flag from GET /models.

3. The automatic reply when a file opens. Kenneth went with the suggestion from the main session's message: app-started turns (the file-opened report, slice-finished note, skills) run on Expert because they need the render, cost 0 credits as rule 2 already says, and do not pin the chat. The chat's model is fixed by the person's first message, and the greyed pickers follow that. In code: use_chat_model does not store the choice when the turn's origin is the app, and the app turn uses the account's Expert alias directly. A chat may therefore have one Expert turn before Standard ones; the gateway strips the images from that history for the Standard model.
</cross-session-message>

The brainstorm session [JusPrin pricing model brainstorm](#local_7448b3b2-e5e7-41e6-bd7d-8389f145dddf) relayed your three decisions, and both working docs now carry them.

**Standard, not Basic.** Every "Basic" in `pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md` and `pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md` is now "Standard". The code tokens stay as they were, since they are identifiers the person never sees: the alias id `slicer-basic`, the tier value `basic` in the alias config, and the `basic_only` flag on trickle lots. The plan notes that the config value stays `basic` while the label reads "Standard".

**A picture in a Standard chat.** Recorded as decided in the design doc's point 2 and the plan's section 5.2: the picker option stays short, the staged attachment row carries the notice "Standard can't see pictures, so this one will not be sent.", a "New Expert chat" button sits beside Remove and carries the typed text and the attachment, Send stays enabled, and a Standard chat lists no picture-returning tools to the model. The new board is "Credits · 3e · Picture in a Standard chat", placed after 3d on the Compositions page. Three captures are above: 3e, and 2b and 3d after the rename. **One new question** the board raised, now in both docs' open lists: a picture staged in a new Standard chat, before the first message, when the picker still works. There the person can simply switch the picker, so the row might need only the sentence rather than the full "New Expert chat" button. That state is not drawn.

Kenneth Jiang 2026-10-06 18:47:26 -0700
Add the local first-run onboarding flow to Home

A new user now gets a short guided path into a first project instead of
landing on an empty Home screen. The path needs no account and no Agent:
welcome, import presets from an existing OrcaSlicer install, confirm or
choose a printer setup, then open a project or the bundled example.

How it works
- The native side decides which step is due. OnboardingModel is a pure
  function from saved progress plus three facts (user presets exist, a
  usable printer is selected, a project is open) to the next step.
  OrcaHomeBackend supplies the facts and stores progress in the app
  config under "jusprin_onboarding".
- The Home page draws the step it is told to draw (Onboarding.tsx). The
  eight screens follow the Figma frames on the "On boarding experience"
  page; at 1280x800 the main block of each lands on its frame's
  rectangle.
- The Home bridge stays on protocol version 1. The new state and
  messages are additive and announced through an "onboarding" entry in
  the capabilities list.

What the page shows is what the app reported
- The Figma frames carry sample data (an example source, example preset
  rows, a sample failure reason). None of it is repeated: preset names,
  counts, and the copied and not-copied lists come from the host, and a
  line the host cannot back is left out.
- The three preset-kind checkboxes control what is imported, and
  "Review selection" lists the preset names found in the Orca folder.
- A failed action is reported: on the project step as the recovery
  card, where Retry repeats the action that failed, and on other steps
  as a line above the buttons.

Deliberately not built
- Account and Agent setup. "Set up JusPrin" and "Set up with Agent" are
  links that open jusprin.com/account.
- The four dropdowns on the setup confirmation show the current value
  only; changing one goes through "Change or find printer".
- Two sizes follow the token file where Figma differs: the close button
  is 26 px (Figma 32) and the breadcrumb chevron 16 px (Figma 14).

Tokens: component.onboarding gains the frame widths (content 960, card
480, example panel 472, setup field 220), guarded in
test_brand_tokens.cpp. Home now also emits the checkbox, select, and
form-row tokens as CSS variables.

Verified: Home page tests (70), jusprin_tests (584 assertions), and
brand_tokens_tests pass. Every screen was captured from the built app on
isolated data folders and compared with Figma.

Not verified end to end: a real import that leaves some presets behind
(the partial-result screen was shown from a stored result), and the
change that keeps the user on Home when the bundled example fails to
open. The failure was reproduced before the change; the corrected
behaviour was not demonstrated.

## 9. Sign-in, accounts and the v1 free quota

- The sign-up lot is created on first contact (3.5), so no change to the OAuth flow.
- v1's `JusPrinAICredit` keeps serving the v1 app. The v2 gateway stops calling `consume_credit_for_pipeline`; its `quota_exhausted` code stays in `errors.py` for v1 compatibility but is no longer raised by v2.
- Account deletion: `can_account_be_deleted` in `app_ent.models` blocks deletion while a prepaid detection-hour pack exists; credit lots should not block deletion (unused credits are forfeited, said on the page).

## 10. Measuring it
## 11. Order of work and tests

1. **Ledger and charging** (gateway + obico-server migration): tables, `charge_turn`, draw order, lazy trickle, sign-up lot, `credits_exhausted` 402 body, `tier`/`credits`/`images` in aliases, `slicer-basic` alias with image stripping, `/account`. Tests in `web_ent/jusprin/v2/tests/`: draw order (expiring first, basic-only skipped for expert, never-expiring last), idempotent charge on a retried first request, two concurrent first requests of different turns against one lot (`select_for_update`), expiry at the boundary, free app turns and their daily cap, the 402 body, image stripping only for `images: false`, and a `/models` response carrying prices. Gateway test harness pattern: `test_gateway.py` with the MockTransport injection the file already uses.
2. **App:** `X-JusPrin-Request: note`, `credits` in `ModelOptionInfo` and the pickers with "a message", pickers greyed once a chat has a message from the person with the tooltip, app-started turns on the Expert alias without storing the chat's model, the attachment row's picture notice and "New Expert chat" button, picture tools left out of a Standard chat's tool list, the `/account` fetch, the ring and hover panel, the pre-send check with "Get more credits" and the conditional "New Standard chat", the failed card, the webview that opens the served Account and pricing page (5.4). Vitest for the page (`ModelPickers.test.tsx`, a new `BalancePanel.test.tsx`, a composer test for the disabled Send and its line), Catch2 for `ProviderAgent`'s header and 402 handling, a Catch2 test that an app-started turn in a fresh chat leaves `chat_model` unset and the next person's message sets it, a Vitest for the attachment row in a Standard chat, one live end-to-end run through the shell harness against staging (`app-stg.obico.io` runs the same image) at a stated spend.
3. **Chargebee and the served pages:** plans, add-ons, coupon, checkout views, webhook branches, the Account and pricing page with the `webview_session` login (5.4), v1-subscriber carry-over. Tests with recorded webhook payloads, including a repeated `subscription_renewed` (no double lot), a cancellation mid-term (lot keeps its expiry), an `invoice_generated` for the pack, and the Obico-cancel coupon removal. Staging run with Chargebee's test site before production.
4. **Cost prerequisites:** 1-hour ttl in `prepare()` (test: the body sent upstream carries `ttl` on every `cache_control`; live check of cache write counts across a 10-minute pause), then the polling guard (host test: third refused poll ends the turn; the slice-finished note turn still runs).
5. **Rewards:** endpoint, storage, admin, the Print history button and form, the Home card line. Tests: duplicate hash rejected, text too short rejected, daily cap, invalid review claws back once and shows its reason in `activity`.
6. **Alert and auto-reload and launch bonus:** suggestion maths with unit tests on the four cases (Pay as you go cheaper, Hobby cheaper, Workshop cheaper, Obico discount flips the answer); auto-reload task with a failed payment path; `JUSPRIN_LAUNCH_DOUBLE_UNTIL`.

# Handoff: build JusPrin Cloud credits and finish the first-run onboarding

Written 2026-11-02 for a coding agent who has not seen the design sessions. This is a working doc: keep it untracked, never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Kenneth tracks unfinished work by the untracked files in `git status`.

## 1. What you are building, in one paragraph

JusPrin 2 is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an in-app AI agent. The agent can run on the person's own API key (free, no account) or on JusPrin's hosted gateway (an Obico-server endpoint, `app.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2/…`, live in production since 2026-10-25). The gateway is about to start charging in credits: a Standard message costs 1 credit, an Expert message 5. People get 500 credits in their first month, can buy packs that never expire, or subscribe (Hobby $10, Workshop $20). This work adds the credit ledger and charging to the gateway, the balance, prices and pre-send checks to the app's composer, the Account and pricing pages, print-report rewards, and finishes the first-run onboarding flow that a month-old branch started. Nothing of this is built yet; the design is done and reviewed.

## 2. Read these first, in this order

1. `pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md` (same folder). The whole technical plan: ledger tables, the charging algorithm, the `/account` JSON, the 402 body, alias config, Chargebee, rewards, section 11 "Order of work and tests", section 12 "Decisions still Kenneth's". Build from it.
2. `pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md`. Each point where a person meets credits, the five rules that apply everywhere, and the exact wording. When the plan and this doc disagree on words, this doc wins.
3. The boards. Captures in `design-captures/credits-2026-11/` (one PNG per board, `credits-<board>-<slug>.png`, `-dark` variants where they exist). `MANIFEST.md` there lists every board with its canvas page and name; `CHANGELOG-v54-to-v69.md` records why each board looks the way it does. The live canvas is the JusPrin v2 design artifact, https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, at version 71. Figma is retired; do not design from it.
4. `AGENTS.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `fork-stewardship.md`, `design-system.md`. House rules; the ones that bite most often are repeated in section 7 below.

## 3. Where the code lives

**App (this repository).** Branch `jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4`, in sync with `origin`. Work in your own worktree and branch; never reuse another session's worktree.
- Composer, pickers, attachments, Preferences page: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/` (`Composer.tsx`, `ModelPickers.tsx`, `AttachmentChip.tsx`, `Preferences.tsx`, `WelcomeBack.tsx`).
- Host side of the agent: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` (`AgentHost.cpp` holds `chat_model_choice`, `use_chat_model`, `start_turn`; `ProviderAgent` sends the gateway headers and maps HTTP errors; `CloudAccount.cpp` and `ModelCatalog.cpp` hold the account's model list).
- Home page and onboarding: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/` and `HomeUI/src/`. Preferences window: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Preferences/`. The v1 import and the welcome-back window: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/V1Import/`.
- Tests: Catch2 under `tests/jusprin/` and `tests/brand/`; Vitest beside each TypeScript file; the shell harness under `tests/shell/` drives the built app without a screen.
- Build: `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all -- -j4`. The Mac is shared by several agent sessions: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, one build per build directory, never restart a running build. Editing a CMake file rebuilds everything.

**Gateway (tsd-enterprise).** Repository `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, branch from `master` (it moved 12 commits past the gateway merge, including the Python 3.12 / Django 5.2 bump), in your own worktree. The gateway is `web_ent/jusprin/v2/` (`aliases.py`, `upstream.py`, `gateway.py`, `stream.py`, `credits.py`, `auth.py`, `errors.py`, `views.py`, `urls.py`; tests in `tests/test_gateway.py` and `tests/test_aliases.py`, using the MockTransport injection the file already uses). `obico-server` is a git submodule: never stage or commit a submodule change. The local stack from the previous session is compose project `jusprin-cloud` on port 3434 (`docker-compose.local-ports.yml` in `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise-worktrees/jusprin-cloud`, whose `LOCAL_TEST_ACCOUNT.txt` holds a test account), with `web_ent/scripts/jusprin/fake_upstream.py --port 8765` standing in for the model vendor. The session cookie is scoped to `.localhost`, so pass it as a header from scripts.

**Deployment (ops).** `~/Projects/ops`: the alias ConfigMap is `tsd/prod/jusprin-v2-gateway.yaml` and `tsd/stg/jusprin-v2-gateway.yaml`. Staging is `https://app-stg.obico.io` and runs the same image as production. Production is live for real users: do not change it. For any `gcloud` or `kubectl` command, first run `gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, and stay read-only on production.

## 4. Step 0: the onboarding branch

`onboarding-frontend-only` (one commit, `8f4588beae`, Kenneth, 2026-10-06; `origin/onboarding-frontend-only` is identical) adds the local first-run path to Home: welcome, import presets from an existing OrcaSlicer install, confirm or choose a printer setup, open a project or the bundled example. Its commit message is a good spec of what it does and what it deliberately left out. It is 139 commits behind `jusprin-newui`.

A dry-run rebase on 2026-11-02 conflicted in 18 of its 27 files. Expect to resolve `HomeBackend.hpp`, `HomeHost.cpp`, `HomeHost.hpp`, `HomeSnapshot.hpp`, `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`, `OrcaHomeBackend.hpp`, `resources/jusprin/home/protocol.json`, `HomeUI/src/App.tsx`, `App.test.tsx`, `bridge/protocol.ts`, `bridge/protocol.test.ts`, `state/store.ts`, `styles.css`, `styles.test.ts`, `tokens.ts`, `sources.cmake`, `tests/jusprin/test_home_host.cpp` and `test_home_snapshot.cpp`. Nine files apply cleanly, among them the three new ones (`OnboardingModel.cpp/.hpp`, `Onboarding.tsx`, `test_onboarding_model.cpp`). What changed underneath: the Home v3 page (`dbec3e3a38`), Print history (`ebbb2f8894`), JusPrin's own Preferences window (`641c17f13e`), every opened file becomes a new project (`d921c4b3dd`), the token sync (`7671e48504`). Most conflicts should be two additive hunks in the same place; keep both.

After the rebase, bring the flow to the current design:
- The canvas's "On boarding experience" page is the source of truth. The branch followed Figma frames; check each of its eight screens against the canvas before trusting its layout.
- Boards 1a to 1d add the first-month offer as the headline on its own surface: "Your first month: 500 credits", under it "That is 500 Standard or 100 Expert messages. Your own API key stays free.", button "Sign in for 500 credits", "Explore first" below. 1a is the setup row in Preferences › Agent over a first-run Home, 1b the welcome screen, 1c the welcome-back window the app already builds for a returning v1 user (signing in is the primary button there), 1d that window once a v1 subscriber has signed in. Never the word "trial"; no dollar figure.
- The branch's "Set up JusPrin" and "Set up with Agent" links to jusprin.com/account go away: since 2026-10-23 every entry point to agent setup opens Preferences › Agent.
- The branch left two paths unverified in the real app: a preset import that leaves some presets behind, and staying on Home when the bundled example fails to open. Show both before calling the step done.

## 5. Then the credits work, in the plan's order

Section 11 of the plan has the steps and their tests. Summary of what each needs and what it waits on:

| Step | What | Waits on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gateway ledger and charging, the `slicer-basic` alias with image stripping, `/account`, the 402 body | Nothing. Start here on the server side. |
| 2 | App: prices in the pickers, pickers greyed after the person's first message, app-started turns on Expert without fixing the chat's model, the attachment row's picture notice, the ring and hover panel, the pre-send check, the failed card | Step 1's `/account` and 402 shapes, which the plan fixes already. The webview that opens Account and pricing waits with step 3. |
| 3 | Chargebee plans, add-ons, coupon, webhooks; the Account and pricing pages; v1-subscriber carry-over | Kenneth's decisions 12 (pages served into a webview, or built in the app), 10 (domain) and the open parts of 8 (when v1 subscribers move, how to word it). Do not start the pages until he has answered. |
| 4 | Cache ttl and the slice-polling guard | Nothing. |
| 5 | Print-report rewards: endpoint, storage, admin review, the Print history button and form, the Home card line | Nothing; Print history exists on `jusprin-newui`. |
| 6 | Savings alert, auto-reload, launch bonus | Steps 1 and 3. |

Steps 0, 1, 2, 4 and 5 can be built now. Steps 1 and 2 can run in parallel in different repositories.

## 6. Decisions you must not make yourself

The plan's section 12 lists them. The ones with a recommended or placeholder answer written in the plan (default tier, alias ids, the 50-a-day cap, the 50-credit trickle, the 600 ceiling, the 25-credit reward, the launch discount form, bars and the ring's total, "New Standard chat", the picture in a new chat, the thinking picker on Standard) you build as written and flag in your report. The ones with no answer (webview or in-app pages, the domain, v1 move timing and wording, Pix) you leave alone and ask Kenneth. If a board, the design doc and the plan disagree, say so rather than picking.

## 7. Rules that bite

- **Words.** The cheap tier is "Standard" everywhere a person reads (the config value stays `basic`, the alias id `slicer-basic`, the flag `basic_only`). Prices always carry their unit: "1 credit a message", never "1 credit". "Your first month", never "trial". Only messages the person sends cost credits. "Get more credits" is the one action outside the pricing page. A file is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". Text the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards some of this; extend it when you add model-facing text.
- **Design tokens.** Every colour, radius, font and control size in UI code comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables (`agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, "Writing UI code"). A value with no token gets a token and a guard first. The two-line tooltip on board 2c needs a design-system change, since tooltips are one line today.
- **OrcaSlicer-owned files.** Read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching anything outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Changes there are small, additive, and come with the rebase evidence that document asks for.
- **Errors.** Do not catch what you cannot recover from; never turn an impossible state into a silent no-op; one generic error for rare failures. Section "Error handling discipline" in `AGENTS.md`.
- **Tests.** Every behaviour change gets a test, and the real app must be exercised for anything a test cannot cover. Reproduce a bug in the real app before fixing it; a failing fake is not a reproduction.
- **Model spend.** No live-model run (the shell harness against a real provider, the live prompt suite) without Kenneth approving that batch and its stated spend. The staging gateway at `app-stg.obico.io` counts.
- **Git.** Commit only when asked; never commit submodule pointers; no attribution lines in commits or PR descriptions; working docs like this one stay untracked.

## 8. How you will know it works

- Gateway: the pytest list in plan section 11 step 1, plus one end-to-end run through the local compose stack with `fake_upstream.py`: sign-up lot created on first contact, a Standard turn charges 1 from the expiring lot first, an Expert turn skips basic-only credits, the 402 body carries `basic_only_credits`, an app-origin turn charges 0.
- App: Vitest for `ModelPickers`, the new balance panel, the composer's disabled Send, the attachment row in a Standard chat; Catch2 for `ProviderAgent`'s headers and 402 handling and for an app-started turn leaving the chat's model unset until the person's first message; the Home and onboarding suites from the branch; one shell-harness run against staging at a spend Kenneth approves.
- Report in four parts, under 500 words: the problem, what you built, what you tested and how, what remains. Say plainly what you did not verify.

=== VM memory
---
name: windows-gui-test-vm-gcp
description: Working recipe for testing the OrcaSlicer/JusPrin GUI headlessly on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP, and the four traps that make it fail silently.
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Windows GUI test VM for this app works in GCP with no GPU. Instance
`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`,
n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB, Cascade Lake), 500 GB pd-balanced,
Windows Server 2022. Harness + full README live outside the repo
at `/Users/kenneth/jusprin-win-vm-harness/`. Verified 2026-09-07 end to end:
launch, screenshot, scripted click, verify the UI advanced.

**Why:** four failure modes here are silent — they look like "the app has no
window" or "the app hung" rather than reporting an error, so they cost hours if
rediscovered from scratch.

**How to apply:**
- OpenGL: the app hard-requires 3.2 and Windows software rendering is 1.1. Drop
  Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` beside the .exe. Then force
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — otherwise Mesa picks
  its d3d12 backend (the GCE virtual display exposes a D3D12 device) and crashes
  on the first frame.
- Never copy the whole Mesa .7z to the VM: Defender deletes it as
  Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere, copy only those, and
  no AV exclusion is needed.
- Session isolation is the big one: display APIs, EnumWindows and
  MainWindowTitle only see the calling session's window station, so over SSH they
  report nothing and it reads as "no window exists". Run anything UI-touching as a
  scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive`.
- Auto-logon must be re-applied on every boot; the GCE image clears the Winlogon
  values after the boot that sets them.
- Resolution needs `gcloud compute instances update --enable-display-device`

The coding session [Build JusPrin Cloud credits and finish onboarding](#local_e414326c-078d-41e3-a9ec-8d8337978b8e) has finished. I checked its three worktrees: the changes are there and nothing is committed. The app branch `claude/credits-onboarding` has 78 modified and 11 new files, the gateway branch `claude/credits-ledger` has 11 modified and 5 new files, and the ops branch `claude/credits-gateway-config` has 4 modified files.

**What it built.** Onboarding is ported to jusprin-newui with the first-month offer as the headline, and every setup entry opens Preferences › Agent. The gateway has the ledger, charging, the Standard alias with image stripping, the account endpoint, the 402 body and print-report rewards. The app has prices in the pickers, pickers greyed once a chat starts, free app-started turns on Expert, the picture notice, balance ring and panel, the pre-send check, the failed-message card, the 1-hour cache ttl, the slice-polling guard, and the Print history report form. It also found and fixed two bugs in the old onboarding branch: saved progress recorded every field as true, and a failed import retry lost the partial-import screen. Step 3 (Chargebee, Account and pricing pages, v1 carry-over) was not started, as briefed.

**What it tested.** All Catch2 suites, both Vitest suites and the 123 gateway tests pass. The shell harness passes in default and print-history modes, after it fixed harness defects that crashed print-history on the base commit too. The real app was driven by a script injected into the page against a local gateway and fake upstream, covering onboarding, credits charging, a free app turn, a real 402 and a stored print report with a 25-credit grant. No live model was run.

**Not verified.** Pointer hover, native file dialogs, the manual setup wizard, completing sign-in, pressing Get more credits, boards 1d and 3e beyond unit tests, Windows, Linux, dark mode, and anything against live providers.

**Decisions it left for you.**
- Which printer the bundled example uses on a fresh install, since "I don't have a printer here" always refuses with no printer installed.
- Whether to deploy before step 3, since the gateway already reports a v1 subscription and board 1d would then show a Hobby price billing has not moved people to.
- Whether to approve three staging chats, estimated under $2, to check an Expert-to-Standard crossing, a free file-open turn and the cache ttl.

Two things to know before deploying: the OpenRouter key secret must exist on the gateway before the ops change is applied, or pods will not start, and after a 402 the composer note also shows, so "Get more credits" appears twice where board 3c shows only the card. Its placeholder choices, doc disagreements and leftover scratch paths are in the notes file at `/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_756f4482-e5c7-45b4-bc36-5e6db3b079ef/credits-onboarding-flags.md`. A ninja build is still running on the Mac, but it belongs to a different worktree, connection-skill, not to this work.

> Which printer the bundled example uses on a fresh install, since “I don’t have a printer here” always refuses with no printer installed.
> Whether to deploy before step 3, since the gateway already reports a v1 subscription and board 1d would then show a Hobby price billing has not moved people to.
> Whether to approve three staging chats, estimated under $2, to check an Expert-to-Standard crossing, a free file-open turn and the cache ttl.

I either don't understand the question or I don't understand why this is a question for me. Also, I don't understand why you want to do live chat. This onboarding process doesn't involve any live chats, right?

You're right to push back. Two of those three are not your decisions, and I relayed them without checking. Here is what each one actually is.

**The example printer.** Onboarding's "I don't have a printer here" path opens the bundled example project. On a fresh install no printer preset is installed yet, so the open fails and the step refuses. That is a bug in the ported branch, not a product choice. The example 3MF carries its own printer and process settings, so the fix is for that path to install what the file needs and then open it. My hypothesis, not verified: the old branch never saw this because it was only tested on data folders that already had a printer. I'll have the session fix it rather than ask you which printer.

**Deploying before step 3.** The gateway already tells the app whether the account has a v1 subscription, and the ported welcome-back screen uses that to promise "Hobby at your original price". Billing has not moved anyone yet, since step 3 is not built. The engineering answer is plain: the app does not show that promise until step 3 ships. Nothing for you to decide. I'll have the session gate the box.

**The live chats.** You're correct that onboarding has no live chat. The request came from the credits part, step 2. Three paths depend on a real provider and the fake upstream cannot exercise them:
- An app-started turn runs on Expert, which is Anthropic. If the person then picks Standard, which is DeepSeek through OpenRouter, the saved history has to be converted between the two providers' message formats before the next request. Only a real reply shows whether that conversion produces a request the provider accepts.
- The free file-opened turn, charged 0, needs a real reply to confirm the ledger stays unchanged end to end.

content.text:
It was me. The design doc's rule 1 says every balance is shown translated, "612 credits left. That is 612 Standard or 112 Expert messages", with my reasoning "so nobody converts in their head". The design session drew it on the panel (board 2a), the welcome screen (1b), the welcome-back window (1d) and every pricing card, and the coding session built exactly that in `BalancePanel.tsx`. You decided "credits" as the unit on 2026-11-01. You never decided the translation line; it rode along in my draft and survived your board reviews without being called out.

I agree it is confusing. Two numbers for one balance, and the second one changes meaning depending on which tier you pick, so a person has to hold both anyway.

There is one place messages are hard to avoid: the free lot. "50 free Standard messages a month" is credits that can only buy Standard, so it is a different kind of thing from the 612. If the display is credits only, that lot needs a credits name too, something like "Free Standard credits · 50 of 50 left · Standard only".

My pick: drop the "That is N Standard or N Expert messages" sentence everywhere (panel, 1b, 1d, pricing cards, Account), keep the one explanation of prices on the pricing page ("A Standard message is 1 credit and an Expert message is 5"), and rename the free lot to credits. Say yes and I'll update the design doc and plan, have the design session change the boards, and have the coding session strip it from the code.
Where do you think are the places where the user needs to know such info so that they won't be confused?

The person needs the translation at exactly the moments they choose or are stopped, and nowhere else. A balance is not one of those moments.

- **The picker, when choosing a tier.** The price sits on the option itself: "Standard · 1 credit a message", "Expert · 5 credits a message". This is where the comparison happens, so this is where both prices belong, side by side. Nothing else on the composer.
- **The moment a message can't be sent.** The card says what this chat costs and what they have: "This Expert chat needs 5 credits a message. You have 3 credits left." The person is deciding what to do next and needs the arithmetic done for them once, for this chat's tier only, not for both.
- **The pricing page, once.** One sentence at the top, "A Standard message is 1 credit and an Expert message is 5. Only messages you send cost credits.", then cards priced in credits. People arrive here to buy and need to know what a credit is worth. It's also the one place a link from the panel can send them for the explanation.
- **The first-month offer, with care.** "Your first month: 500 credits" means nothing to someone who has not seen a price yet. One short line under it, "An Expert message is 5 credits", gives the scale without a second balance. I'd leave the translated total ("500 Standard or 100 Expert messages") out even here.

Everywhere else the person is reading, not deciding: the balance panel, the Account bars, the welcome-back window, the usage table. There the number is credits, full stop. The free lot is named by what it is, "Free Standard credits · 50 left · Standard only", so the only extra fact in the panel is which tier a lot can pay for, not a second count.

The low-balance notice is the one borderline case. "About 5 Expert messages left" is a message count, but it appears once, in the chat that is about to hit the wall, and the person needs to know how many more turns they get in this chat, not what a credit is. I'd keep it.
Okay, I agree. Change the boards accordingly Afterwards, show me the screenshots of your changed board so that I can review.
I'll have the design session, which owns the canvas, make the board changes and re-render the captures, and update the two design docs here meanwhile.

- **Balance panel (2a, and the same panel on 4a to 4c):** the headline is "612 credits left" alone. The free lot is now "Free Standard credits · 50 of 50 left" with "Standard only · Resets 1 Dec" under it.

- **Pricing page (5a, 5b):** no card repeats the price in messages. The one sentence at the top stays. The launch offer now ends "$10 buys 1,000 credits."

The design session is still changing three more that it flagged after the first pass: the 6a composer line becomes "50 free Standard credits this month", the 3d notice says "Your free Standard credits can only pay for Standard", and board 0's rule 1 is reheaded "One word, one unit, credits only." The pricing footer "Everyone also gets 50 free Standard messages a month" and Workshop's "up to 600" stay as they are, since they describe an allowance, not a balance.

The design doc, plan and handoff brief at the repo root say the same now, with a note that the translation was my addition and your decision on 2026-11-02 removed it. The coding session has not been told yet, since its balance panel and welcome screens still carry the old sentence.
Changes first
Which changes? Tell me what's off on which board and I'll send it to the design session.
[Request interrupted by user]

Why is it still "standard credits" and "expert credits"? the credit uisage  Progress bars should be grouped only by when the credits expire. Why doesn't pay as you go credits  not have a progress bar? I'm now seriously worried that we are not on the same page in terms of what the pricing plan was. rephrase to meet your understanding so that I can be sure.

Here is the pricing plan as I understand it. Where a point came from me or the design session rather than from you, I say so.

**One kind of credit.** A credit is worth about 2 cents. A Standard message costs 1 credit, an Expert message costs 5. Any credit pays for either tier. Only messages the person sends cost credits. The app's own turns are free.

**Ways to get credits.**
- First month after sign-in: 500 credits, which expire a month later.
- Pay as you go: $10 buys 500 credits, and they never expire. Launch offer doubles the pack.
- Hobby: $10 a month for 750 credits that reset each month and don't carry over.
- Workshop: $20 a month for 1,000 credits that reset each month, plus unlimited Standard messages up to a placeholder ceiling of 600, after which Standard costs 1 credit.
- Print report reward: 25 credits per accepted report, never expire.
- Obico subscribers: 20% off the plans.
- v1 subscribers: Hobby at their original price, plus the 500 first-month credits.

**Spending order.** Credits that expire soonest are spent first, so bought credits are the last to go.

**What the person sees.** A balance is one number of credits. The panel under it shows one bar per expiry group: credits expiring on a date, credits resetting on a date, credits that never expire. Each bar shows what is left of what was granted.

**Where I diverged from you.** Two things on the boards are not from the plan above:
- The "Free Standard credits · Standard only" lot. The plan carried a placeholder of 50 Standard-only credits a month for everyone, as a free tier that never ends. That lot is the only reason "Standard credits" and "Expert messages" ever appear in a balance. I don't find it in your words. If it is not your intent, it goes, and every credit is the same.
- Bought credits with no bar. That was the design session's recommendation, you asked why, and it never got an answer. Under the plan above they get a bar like the others, "500 of 500 left · Never expire".

If this is right, say so and I'll have both the Standard-only lot and the missing bar removed from the boards, the docs and the code. If the free Standard allowance is something you do want, tell me and I'll keep it, but then it needs its own clear shape.

* Workshop: $20 a month for 1,000 credits that reset each month, plus unlimited Standard messages up to a placeholder ceiling of 600, after which Standard costs 1 credit. - no ceiling. It's probably easier just to say standard messages cost 0 credits
* he “Free Standard credits · Standard only” lot. The plan carried a placeholder of 50 Standard-only credits a month for everyone, as a free tier that never ends. That lot is the only reason “Standard credits” and “Expert messages” ever appear in a balance. I don’t find it in your words. If it is not your intent, it goes, and every credit is the same. - let's just give free users 50/mo use-it-or-loose it credits 
*

Two decisions, recorded. The Standard-only lot and the Workshop ceiling go, free accounts get 50 credits a month that expire, and bought credits get a bar. I'll push that to the boards and the docs, then show you the result.
